design_rationale: Participants were randomly assigned on a 1:1 basis using a web-based randomization service (Sealed Envelope) with stratified permuted blocks.

domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Patients were randomly assigned on a 1:1 basis (www. sealedenvelope.com) into either the conservative or control group, stratified by study site, using random permuted blocks of different sizes.

domain_judgments.rationale: Blinding of clinicians and carers was not possible, and a protocol amendment mid-trial altered the control condition's target, with multiple clinician-initiated withdrawals due to concerns regarding assigned oxygenation targets.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data for primary feasibility endpoints were complete for all 34 participants, and missingness for clinical secondary outcomes (e.g., 30- and 90-day survival) was very low and balanced between arms.

domain_judgments.rationale: Feasibility metrics and objective clinical outcomes such as mortality, ICU stay duration, and physiological oxygenation measures are objective and unlikely to be influenced by lack of blinding of clinical staff, with data analysis conducted blinded.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Data analysis was conducted blinded to specific group allocation. Primary and secondary outcome measures were presented using summary statistics. Missing data, non-compliers and withdrawals were analysed to determine if was bias seemed likely.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial had a pre-published trial protocol and statistical analysis plan, and reported the specified primary feasibility endpoints and secondary clinical outcomes in accordance with the pre-planned analyses.

overall_summary: The study was well-conducted with sound random allocation and transparent reporting of feasibility and clinical outcomes, but open-label delivery of oxygen targets alongside a major mid-trial protocol amendment changing the control group parameters introduces some concerns in Domain 2.

design_rationale: Participants were randomly assigned to groups using a computerized random-number generator with allocation sequence concealed in sequentially numbered, closed, opaque envelopes.

domain_judgments.rationale: A computerized random-number generator was used with allocation concealed in sequentially numbered, opaque envelopes, and baseline differences between groups were consistent with chance.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: On inclusion, patients were randomized by a computerized random-number generator into a low SpO2 group or a high SpO2 group. The randomization sequence was concealed in sequentially numbered, closed, opaque envelopes that were opened after patient study inclusion.

domain_judgments.rationale: Patients were unaware of group assignment, protocol-consistent adjustments in FiO2 were part of routine clinical protocol, an intention-to-treat analysis was performed, and there is no evidence of deviations from the intended intervention that biased the objective outcome of mortality.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The treating team was aware of the SpO2 target and adjusted the FiO accordingly, but the included patients were unaware of their treatment group. ... For all randomized patients, an intent-to-treat (ITT) analysis was used.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data for the primary outcome (28-day mortality) were available for all 214 randomized participants with no loss to follow-up.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: For the ITT analysis, data from 100 patients in the low SpO2 group and 114 patients in the high SpO2 group were used. ... Follow-up phone calls were made every week after discharge until 28 days after inclusion.

domain_judgments.rationale: Mortality at 28 days is an objective outcome that is highly unlikely to be influenced by lack of blinding of the outcome assessors or treating physicians.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary outcome was 28-day mortality. The secondary outcome was ICU mortality. It is common that in China, patients’ legal surrogates do not want terminal patients to die in the hospital, and they would check out the patients in the agonal stage. domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was conducted in accordance with a pre-specified protocol/registration (POSDOT/NCT02999932), and the predefined primary and secondary outcomes were reported according to an intention-to-treat analysis without evidence of selective reporting.

overall_summary: The study is judged to be at low risk of bias across all five RoB 2 domains. design_rationale: Patients were randomly assigned (1:1) to conservative or usual oxygen therapy using computer-generated random numbers with variable-block randomization via a secure, centralized, Internet-based interface.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence was computer-generated with variable block sizes, concealed via a central web-based system, and baseline characteristics were well-balanced between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: We randomly assigned patients to receive conservative oxygen therapy or usual oxygen therapy using a secure, centralized, Internet-based interface. domain_judgments.rationale: Although clinicians were unblinded due to the nature of the oxygen therapy intervention, care was delivered according to protocol with good separation between groups, and analysis followed an intention-to-treat framework without concerning protocol deviations.

domain_judgments.rationale: Primary outcome data were complete for 100% of the intention-to-treat population after post-randomization consent withdrawals (which were balanced: 16 vs 19).

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome of ventilator-free days and mortality is an objective clinical endpoint that is not prone to detection bias despite clinicians being unblinded.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary outcome was the number of ventilator-free days from randomization to day 28. We defined ventilator-free days as the total number of calendar days or portions of calendar days of unassisted breathing during the first 28 days after randomization. All the patients who had died by day 28 were considered to have had no ventilator-free days.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered, with the protocol and statistical analysis plan published prior to the completion of enrollment, and outcomes were reported in accordance with the prespecified plan.

overall_summary: The ICU-ROX trial was a rigorously conducted, randomized clinical trial with robust allocation concealment, high protocol fidelity, objective primary outcome measurement, complete follow-up for the primary endpoint, and prespecified analyses, resulting in low risk of bias across all domains.

design_rationale: Patients with ARDS were randomly assigned to either conservative or liberal oxygen therapy using stratified computer-generated block randomization.

domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Randomization was stratified according to center, age (<45 years, 45 to 65 years, or >65 years), and severity of respiratory failure evaluated according to the Pao2:Fio2 (≤150 mm Hg or >150 mm Hg), with a PEEP of 5 cm of water and a Fio2 of 60 to 100%. Computer randomization was performed in blocks of four.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although open-label due to the nature of arterial blood gas and oxygen saturation monitoring, co-interventions were protocolized and an appropriate intention-to-treat analysis was performed.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data for the primary endpoint (28-day mortality) were available for all included patients with no post-randomization loss to follow-up.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome was all-cause 28-day mortality, an objective outcome that is not susceptible to measurement or observer bias despite open-label treatment allocation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary outcome was death from any cause at 28 days after randomization among the patients, including those for whom care was limited or withdrawn.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was registered on ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT02713451) with a pre-specified statistical analysis plan, and reported results follow the pre-specified primary and secondary endpoints.

overall_summary: All five RoB 2 domains were assessed as low risk of bias, reflecting sound computer randomization, protocolized interventions, complete follow-up for the objective primary endpoint of 28-day mortality, and alignment with the pre-specified protocol and statistical analysis plan.

design_rationale: The study is a multicenter, stratified, parallel-group randomized clinical trial in which adult ICU patients were randomly assigned to lower or higher oxygenation targets using centralized computer-generated allocation.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although open-label due to the nature of adjusting oxygen titration targets, co-interventions were well-balanced, protocol adherence was monitored, and analyses followed the intention-to-treat principle.

design_rationale: Participants were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to either a restrictive or liberal oxygen target using a web-based system with random permuted blocks.

design_rationale: Participants were randomly allocated using computer-generated permuted block randomization with variable block sizes.

Randomization number and the allocated arm were typewritten in a lighter font on a colored A4 page, which was then folded and inserted in a sequentially numbered opaque envelope for each patient. It was impossible to decipher the allocated arm by holding the envelope against a bright light. All envelopes were sealed and securely stored in a locked cabinet.

domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary endpoint was death from any cause at day 28 after inclusion.

overall_summary: The trial was well-designed and conducted with robust allocation concealment, intention-to-treat analysis, nearly complete follow-up, and an objective primary outcome of 28-day all-cause mortality, resulting in low risk of bias across all RoB 2 domains.
